title: The Pattern
timelinePosition: Day 5 of the hunt from the grain road (Ch5 day count). The party left the carters' lodge at the fork at first light and turned onto the south road. S1 is early morning on the climb, S2 is late morning to early afternoon at the Strahnbrad camp, S3 is the afternoon run to Andorhal, which comes into sight in the last working hours of the day.
openLocation: Southern feeder road into Andorhal's network, with the Strahnbrad military zone ahead.
immediateObjective: Confirm how large the grain-plague plot really is and force someone in Lordaeron's command to take the warning seriously.
constraints: Limited third, absolute: Jaina only. Nothing she cannot see, hear, feel, read or infer. Sylvanas is read from outside.
Register change from Ch5 (paper, ledgers, night road): Ch6 is camp, rank, noise, mud, then a living city. Do not re-run ledger work or the sickroom.

Narration for Sylvanas: Ch5 moved Sylvanas's own narration to 'Jaina' for the mage. Aloud, Sylvanas still says 'Mage' (or 'Proudmoore' in front of others) unless this outline changes it; it does not. Lyriel says 'Jaina'; Cyndia does not.

Jaina's body: right hand dead since Ch2, left hand raw and wrapped with two usable fingertips. Reins and the notes are held in the left hand or against the saddle. No casual inking, no hand-reading. Readings come through spell light, the staff, or pressure in her head. Carry fatigue: little rest since the Ch4 vigil.

Jaina's magical sensitivity is the only way the party perceives contamination. Elves cannot feel it. Sylvanas's question in Beat 7 ('did you read anything off him') is a legitimate use of that and must have a real, quick, honest answer: nothing but a tired clerk.

Arthas is read from outside through behavior, voice, and what others lose around him. Warm, confident, charismatic at Strahnbrad (character sheet), courteous used as a shield. Not cartoon cruelty. Part of his reasoning must be understandable: the orc war is real and visible.
Do not claim Arthas ignores her out of personal cruelty alone. The orc war matters. Do not flatten him into a villain or Jaina into a victim.
No Mal'Ganis naming or recognition. No Kel'Thuzad naming; Jaina's 'someone I once studied with' is a fear she cannot test, not a name.
No certainty that the Barovs designed the plague. Barov paperwork is connection, not guilt (carried from Ch5). Do not re-explain the Barov name or the lost day; they are callbacks.

The farewell ('May the stars keep your road') is a plant: Sylvanas calls it wrong, not yet a pattern. Do not explain it in prose. The tally-man must read as helpful, ordinary, forgettable on the surface.
Cyndia's turned head at the Millhaven carter is held for Ch9. In Beat 7 Cyndia may be present on the road but must not react to or connect the farewell on the page.
Lyriel's Ch3 answer about the carter must not be connected by any character to the farewell, the depot warning, or the tally-man.
Havel is not known to be cult-paid by any character. The party takes him as a militia captain who knows the granary district. The second read is planter-only, never narrated as fact.
Neral is not with the party. She stays on the northbound warning line.
Do not state that all human authority is useless everywhere. It fails here, at this camp, in this hour.
No counted time in dialogue ('two breaths'). Orders by event.

Jaina's ladder (plague-mechanism.md, Ch4-6): she isolates ingestion, repeated exposure and body participation as a design. She still cannot explain how sickness becomes undeath. Do not hand her the 'answering chamber' model or low/high fidelity; that is Ch9-12.
No pre-written dialogue in plan beyond the two locked lines recorded below. The plague line in Beat 1 and the farewell in Beat 7 are authorial anchors from the outline.

Sylvanas carries the evidence at the open. At the Ch5 fork she folded the shared map sheet (knife hole at Strahnbrad) and put it in her coat with the Barov slips and the ANDORHAL sacking square. Any paper Jaina holds up to Arthas has to pass from Sylvanas's coat to Jaina's hand on the page before B4. Jaina holds it in the two bare fingertips of the wrapped left hand or pinned against the staff. She cannot write new notes.

Ch5 closed on a long brown smear moving over the hills, 'too brown for mist'. It is army traffic dust or smoke from the burned farms, never plague. It should resolve as the army by the time the camp is in view (B3). Morning mist low on the road in B1 can sit under it.

Arthas's war is against orcs 'out of the camps' burning farms in the hills. That came from the Ch5 road talk at the south-road inn, and Jaina was at that table. The outline's Blackrock raiders are those orcs. His war is the camps' war, and B5's memory turns on that. The burned farms and the dead are real.

Sylvanas 'knows there is history' only from what she sees (subplot-jaina-arthas.md). The internment-camp memory in B5 stays inside Jaina. She does not tell it to Sylvanas; the Arthas price is told at sea in Ch19.
No named Silver Hand or army officers besides Arthas: no Uther, no Falric. They are not in the outline cast. The Silver Hand is plate and tabards in the camp.
No party member gives a road blessing or an ornate farewell (Lyriel and Cyndia voice-sheet rule). The farewell belongs to the tally-man alone.
The tally-man must not resemble the Ch3 carter: no crooked nose, no hat turned in the hands, no brown cob or flat wagon. He is on foot. His face stays forgettable.

Jaina cannot read people. In Ch5 she read the overseer: 'Nothing on him... No more than on you.' Her 'nothing' in B7 is the same limit. She does not connect the tally-man to the overseer, and she does not know Sylvanas has been turning the carter over since Ch5 (that was Sylvanas's interior).
The river-depot overseer fled south with his wife (Ch5). Do not sight him on this road.

Ch4 already put the built-craft recognition on the page: 'It's made. Somebody very good made this.', the locked shelf in Dalaran, wanting to take it apart, 'as Antonidas built a ward'. S1 is the next step. The whole system is the weapon, with the body inside it, and the fear points at a person trained where she was. Give the Ch4 material brief anchors only. Do not re-run the shelf exposition.

Name usage. Aloud, Jaina says 'Ranger-General' to Sylvanas and 'Arthas' to the prince, from old habit. Arthas says 'Jaina' to her and 'Ranger-General' to Sylvanas. Sylvanas says 'Proudmoore' in front of others and 'Mage' otherwise. To Arthas she uses his correct title, said precisely. Jaina's narration calls her 'Sylvanas'.

povKnowsAtOpen: The cult is organized, watched, and disciplined.
Barov property and paperwork keep turning up in the trail of rot.
Their chosen road runs through the military zone near Strahnbrad before Andorhal.
Her sensitivity has put them ahead of most of Lordaeron, but they are still chasing poison that has already spread.
The old carter from the Millhaven road is still an unresolved road clue in her mind.
They lost a day to a depot overseer's lie.
She can see necromancy in the design but cannot explain how sickness becomes undeath.
povDoesNotKnowAtOpen: Whether the Barovs are fully complicit.
What Andorhal looks like from inside the city.
mustNotBeImpliedYet: No certainty that the Barovs designed the plague.
No claim that Arthas ignores her out of personal cruelty alone. The orc war matters.
No claim that all human authority is useless everywhere rather than failing here.
castKnowsLeavingChapter: Arthas heard the warning and chose the visible war first.
Sylvanas has heard the farewell twice and calls it wrong, not yet a pattern. Jaina got no magical read off the man, and he was gone before Sylvanas looked back.
The plague is deliberate, formally trained craft, with the body part of the mechanism. Origin and ladder height unknown.
A granary tally-man told them to ask for Captain Havel at the militia post by the market gate.
Andorhal looks alive and busy even though the plagued roads run through it.

pov: She opens convinced clear evidence will make Arthas act before Andorhal locks down.
She keeps pushing facts as if proof and rank should matter more than the visible war in front of him.
Arthas hears her out and still turns to the orcs, forcing her to accept Sylvanas was right about the army.
By the end, Jaina stops looking to Lordaeron's command for rescue and turns toward Andorhal itself.

beats: Sylvanas reads the soldiers, the hierarchy, and the coming refusal faster than Jaina does.
Jaina keeps hoping proof will prove Sylvanas too cynical, then watches Sylvanas call the prince's blindness before the conversation is over.
Their argument no longer feels like mage versus soldier. It feels like two women reading the same failure from different angles.

team.label: Partnership
beats: They are still strained, but they are finally working the same problem.
The fight over whether Lordaeron will listen ends here, and their anger turns outward.
They are not gentle with each other yet, but the old prejudice has less room to hide.

castAndHandoffRules: Cyndia: still with the riding party.
Lyriel: still with the riding party.
Neral: not with the party. She remains on the northbound warning line after escorting the survivor girl out.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 7 opens at Andorhal with the same four riders arriving to hunt the poison's source.

factsLocked: Arthas heard the warning and did not act on it the way they needed.
Sylvanas has heard the farewell twice and calls it wrong, not yet a pattern. Jaina got no magical read off the man, and he was gone before Sylvanas looked back.
The party reaches Andorhal by the road chosen in Chapter 5.
A granary tally-man on the road told them to ask for Captain Havel at the militia post by the market gate.
The city still looks alive and busy even though the plague roads run through it.
factsNotEarned: Any claim that all human authority is useless everywhere rather than failing here.

scenes.title: The Pattern on the Road
scenes.sceneFunction: Jaina finally sees the plague as deliberate craft instead of a string of unlucky villages.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: They are on the grain road with the cult trail, the Barov clue, and the chosen approach toward Strahnbrad. Little rest since the Ch4 vigil. Right hand dead, left raw. Ch5's lost day and Barov paperwork are callbacks.
scenes.arcPressure: Jaina's stance test begins here: facts are her tool, and she will carry them to Arthas expecting them to be enough. The pattern recognition also makes the plague personal through forbidden Kirin Tor craft.
scenes.enrichment: Local canon: plague-mechanism.md (grain as carrier, repeated ingestion conditions the body, death completes the lock). Ch6 sits on the ladder rung Ch4-6, isolating ingestion, repeated exposure and body participation without the final step. Jaina recognising craft is on-model: she can recognise brilliance early but lacks the banned frame until Kel'Thuzad gives it names. Sources: stories/the-plague-road/plans/plague-mechanism.md.

beats.goal: Fit the scattered signs into one reading before they reach Strahnbrad: grain routes, dark alchemy, necromancy, and the living body as parts of one thing, so she can state it to the others and, later, to Arthas.
beats.conflict: Each sign has so far looked like a different kind of accident. Her head hurts, the road mist smears the map she is building from the saddle, and the pieces only agree if she stops asking for a single wizard's hand behind them.

outcome.summary: The pieces lock. The plague is a built weapon, too tuned to be harvest luck or a lone wizard's stunt, with the body itself part of the mechanism. She puts it to the others in one plain line. She cannot say who built it or how high the cult ladder goes.

beats.valueShift: chaos of unlucky villages -> deliberate expert design
newOnPageInformation: The plague is a deliberately built weapon: grain routes, dark alchemy, necromancy and the living body working together
Whoever built it had serious formal training
The body is part of the mechanism, not only the victim
Locked line (outline anchor): Jaina says it comes in on the wagons and walks out on its own feet
stillUnknownAfterBeat: How high the cult ladder goes
How sickness becomes undeath (the last step)
sensoryAnchors: the road under the hooves reading heavy, a thin new layer over old (her Ch5 read of this road)
pain climbing behind her eyes
damp road mist low on the climb, and the brown smear over the hills above it
the staff in the crook of the dead arm, its crystal a washed-out gold
the map redrawn in her head from the saddle
beats.interiority: the signs finally agreeing; too tuned for luck, too even for one hand; harvest bad luck was a comfort and it is gone; she says it plainly because plain is the only way it stays true
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas takes the line the way a soldier takes a scouting report. She presses on one weak joint: how does Jaina show this to people who cannot feel it (Ch5: 'You'll have to. I can't see it either.')? That makes the plain line land in company, not only in Jaina's head. Cyndia and Lyriel are present and quiet. Keep the exchange short so the recognition stays the beat.
beats.transitionIntent: sensory-carry: the plain statement leaves Jaina with a second, worse recognition about the quality of the work.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, early morning. The first hours on the south road after the fork, climbing under the hills.
beats.continuityNote: Opening beat and an evolution, not a discovery. Ch4 established that the substance is built ('Somebody very good made this'). Ch4 established ingestion through repeated meals. Ch5 established the regional network and the south road read 'old at the bottom with a thin new layer on top'. The click is those three becoming one weapon, with the body as its last working part. 'Walks out on its own feet' has a referent Jaina knows: Millhaven's dead went north on foot (Ch3). Craft research, epiphany: the realization needs a present-tense trigger and a visible consequence, not a 'she realized' frame. Trigger options already in continuity are the road read under the hooves and the army wagons on the climb; the writer chooses. Consequence: she says it aloud and Sylvanas tests it. The ladder stops short. She cannot explain how sickness becomes undeath.
beats.verifierModification: Resolved the plannerWarning. castFunction now gives Sylvanas a specific pressure point, the 'show it' problem carried from the Ch5 close. Generic 'wet leather' and 'horses cutting through fog' are replaced with continuity anchors: the Ch5 road read, the staff crystal, and the brown smear. Added a guard against re-running the Ch4 material as new.

beats.emotion: Disgust at understanding too much: nausea, white knuckles, pressure buzzing harder in her temples as she recognises real mastery in something that is killing villages.
beats.dilemma: Admit how good the work is and risk wanting to take it apart, or look away from the craft and lose the one edge she has on the people who built it. She cannot tell whether the author is someone she once studied with.
beats.decision: She admits it to herself without comfort and keeps the assessment, because she needs it. She means to put the whole design in front of Arthas, and she believes a clean case will move him before Andorhal is past saving (POV arc bullet 1, carried from Ch5's 'Then I'll have to show it to them'). She rides on toward Strahnbrad with the evidence and a bad taste in her mouth.
beats.valueShift: clear-eyed horror -> complicit fascination she refuses to name
newOnPageInformation: The plague touches forbidden Kirin Tor theory about keeping bodies useful after death
Jaina can recognise craft in it that she would admire anywhere else
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether the work belongs to someone she once studied with
sensoryAnchors: pressure buzzing in her temples
the wrapped left hand clenched on the reins until the split in the palm pulls
nausea
sour spit
mist beading on the staff
beats.interiority: the elegance of it, and wanting to take it apart to see how; that wanting, while villages die of it; the forbidden shelves in Dalaran, and who else read them; not admiration, assessment, and she knows that is a lie
beats.transitionIntent: action continuation: the road climbs out of the mist toward the brown smear and the camp under it. Invisible evidence rides straight into the visible war.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, morning. The same stretch of road, still climbing.
beats.continuityNote: In Ch4 Jaina read one jar letter by letter, thought it beautiful, wanted to take it apart, and measured it against Antonidas's wards. Do not stage any of that as fresh. The new step: the craft is now a whole system, and the fear has a shape, someone trained where she was. It stays a fear with no name (no Kel'Thuzad). One anchor to the locked shelf is enough. Hands: right dead, left wrapped with two bare fingertips, so there are no white knuckles to show.
beats.verifierModification: The decision now carries POV arc bullet 1 explicitly (she believes the case will move Arthas). The plan had it only in S1's arcPressure, and the outline wants the opening beats to show it. 'White knuckles' is replaced because her hands are wrapped and one is dead. The transition now carries the Ch5 smear into B3.

scenes.title: Strahnbrad
scenes.sceneFunction: Jaina gives Arthas the truth and watches him choose the wrong war.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: The party understands the plague's design. Lordaeron's command does not.
scenes.arcPressure: Jaina's central stance test: proof and rank versus the visible war. She must lose it, and accept Sylvanas was right about the army, without cheapening Arthas.
scenes.enrichment: Local canon: arthas.md (Strahnbrad voice: warm, confident, charismatic; flaw: uncertainty experienced as failure; never POV) and subplot-jaina-arthas.md (diagnostic incident on the road to Dalaran: orc internment camp, females and infants, he was adamant the camps were necessary). Camp feel: mud, shouting officers, banners, Silver Hand plate. Geography flag (planner memory of WC3 canon, not verified by web search): Strahnbrad is canonically in the Alterac/Hillsbrad foothills, not directly on the road into Andorhal; the outline places it as the military zone on the southern feeder road. Kept as authorial placement. VERIFIER: Ch5 memory (world/geography, locations/south-road-toward-strahnbrad) already places Strahnbrad in the hills on the south road, before Andorhal's back way in. The placement is established on the page, so the canon flag is closed.

beats.goal: Get to Arthas and secure an audience with the person who can move Lordaeron's strength, using her rank and her history with him.
beats.conflict: The camp is built around the Blackrock raids: mud, shouting officers, banners, and the kind of danger armies like because they can point at it. The army faces the wrong way, and the party is four strangers on elven horses in the middle of it.

outcome.summary: Their route leads straight to Arthas and she gets the audience she needed, under the worst possible conditions: a camp at war footing, not a council.

beats.valueShift: hope in her history with him -> hope tested against what she can see
newOnPageInformation: Lordaeron is pouring its strength into the visible Blackrock threat at Strahnbrad
The camp's posture confirms what Sylvanas predicted about army priorities
The party reaches Arthas without being turned away
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether Jaina's history with Arthas will help or hurt
sensoryAnchors: mud churned by iron tyres and the King's post-horse shoes
officers shouting across banners
wet canvas and horse lines
iron and smoke; burned-farm smoke on the hill line
military press nothing like Farstrider scouting
beats.interiority: the army is facing the wrong way and she can see it before he speaks; Sylvanas said it would; still hoping the proof will show Sylvanas was too cynical, and that the history buys a harder look
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas reads the camp at a soldier's speed before Jaina does: who runs it, where the messengers go, which way the guards face (through-POV bullet 1). Before the audience, the papers pass from Sylvanas's coat to Jaina's hand. Who offers and who asks is the writer's call, but the case is visibly handed to the person who has to make it. Cyndia and Lyriel keep tight on the horses. Silver Hand plate is visible in the camp, unnamed. Arthas uses Jaina's first name in front of the party, and that familiarity is all Sylvanas has to read the history from.
beats.transitionIntent: question-pressure: standing in front of him, Jaina has one case to make and everything riding on how he takes it.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, late morning. The Strahnbrad camp in the hills, on the south road.
beats.continuityNote: Sylvanas's Ch5 prediction ('they'll put the flour after the orcs, and after the horses, and after the quartermaster's supper... Expect them to get in the way') is being tested here, not confirmed in advance. Cyndia's iron-tyred wagons and post-horse shoes are already on the record, and the brown smear resolves into this army. Arthas is on the page for the first time in the book. Before now he was road talk.
beats.verifierModification: Interiority adds Jaina's hope that proof will show Sylvanas too cynical (through-POV bullet 2). castFunction adds the evidence handoff from Sylvanas's coat (continuity: Sylvanas folded the sheet into her coat at the Ch5 close). Sensory anchors are tied to the Ch5 wagon evidence and the burned farms.

beats.goal: Give Arthas the warning cleanly: grain is carrying it, it is organized, and Andorhal is where the routes meet. Make him move before Andorhal locks down.
beats.conflict: He hears every word, stays perfectly courteous, and uses good manners as a shield. His reasons are visible and real: orcs out of the camps, burned farms, dead he can name, a war he can see from the hill. Poisoned grain ranks below that in his reckoning. Before Jaina finishes the case, Sylvanas calls what he will do. It is a prediction made while he can still prove her wrong, and he doesn't.

outcome.summary: Arthas ranks the visible war above the plague and walks away. The warning lands nowhere. Jaina's rank and their history count for nothing, and Sylvanas's call about the prince is on record before the conversation is over.

beats.valueShift: trust in proof and rank -> proof that polite rejection costs lives
newOnPageInformation: Arthas listened fully, was courteous, and still chose the orc war
Maps and notes carry no weight against a battle he can point to
Sylvanas called his blindness before the exchange ended
stillUnknownAfterBeat: How many people will die because he waits
sensoryAnchors: polished armor with camp mud on the greaves
gold hair and the crest
the folded sheet weightless in her two bare fingertips
the knife hole at Strahnbrad in the paper
courtesy used like a shield
beats.interiority: proof should matter; she has the facts in order and he is nodding at them; he heard everything and none of it changed him; Sylvanas is not wrong and she hates that she is right
beats.castFunction: Arthas reads as warm, charismatic and entirely sure. His turn has two parts: he grants the point, then he decides (voice sheet, stage 1). Sylvanas speaks sparingly. Her call lands as a soldier's read of a commander and is aimed at what he will do. It is not the verdict on what he is; that waits for B6. She is not smug.
beats.plannerWarning: Do not write Arthas's cruelty. His reasons must be recognisable: the orcs are a real, visible threat with real dead. The outline asks for courtesy as a shield and no personal cruelty.
beats.transitionIntent: emotional-carry: the refusal leaves Jaina holding paper he never took.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, around midday. In the open at the camp, not in a council tent.
beats.continuityNote: This is the first Jaina-Arthas exchange on the page. Her case is what she has: grain as the carrier, repeated meals, an organized network, the roads converging on Andorhal. The ladder stops short of how sickness becomes undeath. If the Barov name comes up, it is a name and a seal on paper and nothing more. Arthas knows the Barovs as a court house, and Jaina must not accuse. Papers in hand come from Sylvanas's coat (B3). Arthas does not take them.
beats.verifierModification: Conflict now names Arthas's visible reasons (orcs out of the camps, from the Ch5 road talk), so the orc war carries weight. Sylvanas's on-the-spot call is split from B6's verdict: B4 is a prediction, B6 is a diagnosis and Jaina's acceptance, so the same note does not play twice. Anchors are adjusted for one usable hand.

beats.emotion: Anger at him, and at herself for thinking the history would buy a second look. Sour metal at the back of her mouth.
beats.dilemma: Was she unfair to him then, or is she now? Does she keep waiting on his permission and his army, or accept that nobody in Lordaeron's command will carry this for her?
beats.decision: She stops waiting for permission. She will say out loud that Sylvanas called it, and she goes on with the evidence she has.
newOnPageInformation: Years ago on the road to Dalaran Arthas talked Jaina into slipping past the watchtowers of an orc internment camp to look. He was sure the camps were necessary before they reached the fence, and still sure after she had seen the females and infants
Today he was slow, polite, and just as sure
Jaina stops waiting for permission
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether anyone in Lordaeron will believe them before whole cities start dying
sensoryAnchors: sour metal at the back of her mouth
notes still folded the way she held them up
the space where he stood filling with other officers
mud and canvas smell
beats.interiority: sure before the fence, sure after the infants, and today slow and still sure; was she unfair then, or is she now; angry at him, and at herself for thinking the history would buy a second look; Sylvanas called it before she finished, and she will have to say so out loud
beats.transitionIntent: sensory-carry: the empty space he left leads straight into Sylvanas stepping into it.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, around midday. The same spot, moments after he turns away. Flashback: years ago, at night, on the road to Dalaran.
beats.continuityNote: Ch5 ended with Jaina taking the job ('Then I'll have to show it to them'). She showed it, and it failed. That is the evolution. The internment-camp night is on the page for the first time. These are the same camps the Ch5 road talk named ('orcs out of the camps'), so the memory has a live present-day trigger. Craft research, short flashbacks: one moment, one night, entered through something in the present and exited on a present-tense jolt (officers filling the space he left, or Sylvanas). The memory stays interior, and Sylvanas does not hear it.

beats.emotion: Relief that the fight with Sylvanas about whether Lordaeron will listen is over, and an anger that now points outward instead of at each other.
beats.dilemma: Argue the read with Sylvanas one more time, or take it without argument and put the energy into Andorhal.
beats.decision: Jaina accepts Sylvanas's read of Arthas as a military obstacle without needing to teach her the history. They turn the horses back to the road. Andorhal is the only real lead.
beats.valueShift: mage versus soldier -> two women reading the same failure
newOnPageInformation: Sylvanas names the military failure cleanly and Jaina does not fight her on it
Their fight over whether Lordaeron will listen ends here
Andorhal is their only real lead
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether Andorhal will give them proof loud enough to force action
sensoryAnchors: Arthas's absence making the space between them cleaner
Sylvanas cutting to the point
horses wheeling back toward the road
camp noise thinning behind
beats.interiority: saying it out loud costs less than she expected; the history lesson was never what Sylvanas needed; they are not gentle with each other yet, but the old prejudice has less room to hide
beats.transitionIntent: action-continuation: horses wheel back to the road and the lead they have left is the city.
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas's line here is the verdict: what he is, a commander who fights the war he can see. It is not a repeat of B4's prediction. Jaina says aloud that Sylvanas called it, which pays off B5's 'she will have to say so out loud'. Sylvanas does not ask for the history, and Jaina does not offer it. No thanks, and no warmth spoken.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, early afternoon. Leaving the camp for the road.
beats.continuityNote: Sylvanas's Ch5 prediction is now proven, and Jaina concedes it. The Ch5 relationship state was trust spent in acts, not words, and it holds. Jaina still says 'Ranger-General' aloud. Sylvanas still says 'Mage' aloud and never 'Jaina'. Keep the beat short; it follows two heavy beats.
beats.verifierModification: castFunction added. It separates the B6 verdict from the B4 prediction, lands B5's out-loud payoff, and keeps the history interior. Weight set to compressed so the aftermath does not run long.

scenes.title: The Road to Andorhal
scenes.sceneFunction: The old carter clue resurfaces on the road, and Andorhal finally appears.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: Arthas has failed them, and the city is their only remaining lead.
scenes.arcPressure: Jaina's stance after the refusal is to turn toward Andorhal itself instead of Lordaeron's command. The tally-man beat plants a thread she cannot read.
scenes.enrichment: Local canon: lordaeron-and-northrend.md (Andorhal: agricultural nerve center, granaries, loading yards, manifests, wagons, clerks, grain dust, warm dry sweetness, constant labor noise, practical low walls) and supporting.md (Captain Aldric Havel, Andorhal militia captain: harried, honest, solving the wrong scale of problem; he is a planted cult-paid figure in Ch7-8 by the outline's second-read note, which is an authorial divergence from the supporting.md summary and needs reconciliation by the outline owner). Horses: thalassian-horses.md says they settle fast near arcane hum, so skittishness here is a meaningful signal. VERIFIER: the Ch8 outline states that Havel was on cult coin, so the outline chain is consistent; only supporting.md lags. In Ch6 he is a name and a militia post, nothing more.

beats.goal: Get last directions into Andorhal from the first ordinary person walking out of it.
beats.conflict: He is helpful, ordinary, forgettable until his farewell. Sylvanas turns in the saddle at the words and asks whether Jaina read anything off him. Jaina got nothing but a tired clerk. By the time Sylvanas looks back, he is lost in the traffic.

outcome.summary: They get usable directions: ask at the militia post by the market gate for Captain Havel, who knows the granary district. The farewell from Millhaven comes back and leaves Sylvanas with a wrong note she cannot use yet. Twice is wrong, but not yet a pattern. She says so in a few words and rides on.

beats.valueShift: plain courtesy -> a wrong note Jaina cannot read
newOnPageInformation: A granary tally-man walking out of Andorhal with a ledger satchel gave directions
Ask at the militia post by the market gate for Captain Havel, who knows the granary district better than anyone
He glanced back up the road toward Andorhal's granary roofs as he answered
He sent them off with the farewell from Millhaven (locked line: May the stars keep your road)
Sylvanas heard the farewell a second time, asked whether Jaina read anything, and called it wrong but not yet a pattern
stillUnknownAfterBeat: That it is the same being in another face

a ledger satchel, its strap worn pale across his coat

beats.interiority: nothing off him but a tired clerk, and she looked properly, didn't she; Sylvanas turned in the saddle over a turn of phrase; a farewell is a farewell; but she was asked, and had nothing, and dislikes having nothing
beats.castFunction: Sylvanas carries the beat. Cyndia and Lyriel present and silent about the phrase (Cyndia's carter reaction is held for Ch9; Lyriel must not connect anything).
beats.plantedThread: SECOND READ (plant only, prose must not explain): he has just come from checking the granaries where his work is spreading, and he routes the party to his own man. Havel is cult-paid (Ch7-8). While he answers he looks the four riders over again: who rides where, and how far apart. Surface read is clerk's plain courtesy. The look may appear only as a physical detail seen from Jaina's POV, never as inference.
beats.disclosureProvenance: Jaina sees a tired clerk, a glance over his shoulder, and a lingering look at the party that fits a person memorising an unusual group. She does not read it as surveillance. Sylvanas's wrongness is the only flag, and she has no proof.
beats.plannerWarning: Planter and POV tension: the second read is information Jaina does not have. The writer must render the glance and the look as ordinary behaviour (a man sizing up armed strangers on elven horses) and not tilt the narration toward suspicion.
beats.transitionIntent: sensory-carry: the farewell stays with Sylvanas as a wrong note and the road to Andorhal narrows.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, afternoon. The last stretch before Andorhal, with foot and cart traffic thickening on the road.
beats.continuityNote: The wording is fixed: 'May the stars keep your road.' Jaina was present at Millhaven in Ch3, but that was Sylvanas's POV, so Jaina has no on-page memory of the phrase. It reaches her through Sylvanas's turn in the saddle. Jaina does not know Sylvanas has been turning the carter over since Ch5, so the turn looks out of proportion to her. 'Did you read anything' is a real use of Jaina's sense, and the answer is honest: she cannot read people (Ch5, the overseer). She does not draw the overseer parallel herself. Lyriel, who answered the carter in Ch3, connects nothing. Cyndia shows no reaction on the page (held for Ch9). The order of march he looks over: Sylvanas in front, Cyndia on the left, Lyriel on the right at Jaina's knee, Jaina in the middle, two places at the back. Render the look only as a man sizing up armed strangers on elven horses. Craft research, fair play: the clue is on the page, ordinary, and followed at once by something more pressing (B8's body reaction).
beats.verifierModification: Removed 'grain dust on his sleeves'. Jaina reads residue off things that have sat with the grain (Ch5: an emptied store reads 'like a room where somebody's smoked a pipe'), so a man dusted from Andorhal's granaries could not honestly read as 'nothing'. Replaced with a neutral satchel strap. Added the carter-resemblance and overseer-link guards.

beats.goal: Keep riding toward Andorhal while the city's magical rot presses on her.
beats.conflict: The closer they get, the less she can keep the plague at arm's length. The corruption becomes a physical reaction. The horses feel it before the buildings show and go skittish on the narrowing road.

outcome.summary: Jaina keeps riding anyway. The corruption is heavy enough to force a body reaction, and they push on until the city breaks the horizon.

beats.valueShift: theory at a distance -> pain in her body
newOnPageInformation: Andorhal's magical rot stops being theory and hurts Jaina physically
The horses sense it before the buildings are visible
Jaina keeps riding anyway
stillUnknownAfterBeat: Whether Andorhal is already dead behind its walls
sensoryAnchors: pressure behind her eyes
thick, sluggish air
the horses sidestep as at the ring stones and do not settle after

beats.interiority: the plague was theory for most of the road and the road is done arguing with her; she keeps riding because stopping is no different from waiting on permission
beats.castFunction: Thalassian horses are trained to settle near arcane hum (thalassian-horses.md); here they do not settle. Sylvanas and Cyndia work the animals. Lyriel is at Jaina's knee, and when Lyriel checks on her, Jaina keeps going. That is the agency in the beat: stopping would be waiting again.
beats.transitionIntent: action-continuation: they keep riding until the city breaks the horizon.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, late afternoon. The road narrowing into Andorhal's approach, the city not yet in sight.
beats.continuityNote: This is the next rung of the horse ladder. At the ring stones in Ch1-2 they sidestepped once and stood. In Millhaven in Ch3 the mare backed and pinned her ears. Here they sidestep and never settle. It is also the next rung of Jaina's cost ladder from Ch5: teeth chattering, frost on the bare fingertips, the crystal dimming through the day. She can feel Andorhal now only because she is physically arriving; she cannot hear places she has not been (Ch5). Elves still feel nothing themselves. They read it off the horses and off Jaina.
beats.verifierModification: Replaced the vague 'ward-stone-style sidestep' with the established horse-reaction ladder. Added Jaina's Ch5 cost markers. castFunction gives Jaina an act of agency, which breaks up a run of reactive beats in S3.

beats.goal: Reach sight of Andorhal and learn whether it is a ruin or a living city.
beats.conflict: They expected a ruin and the rot and body reaction primed her for one. What she sees is a working city with granaries moving, traffic flowing, ordinary commercial noise and something rotten underneath.

outcome.summary: Andorhal is worse than a ruin: it is working. The plague runs through a living hub, and whoever manages the spread is still inside. Chapter 7 opens with the ride into the city.

The poisoned roads converge on a working hub

beats.interiority: the city looks alive and that is the horror; they were chasing something that had already spread, and it was running; whoever manages it is still in there; nobody behind her is coming, and the city is the thing in front of her
beats.transitionIntent: planted question: who inside the walls is running it. Chapter 7 (Sylvanas POV) opens with the ride in and the one name they have, Captain Havel at the market-gate militia post.
beats.timeAnchor: Day 5, late afternoon into the last working hours. Granaries and traffic still moving.
beats.continuityNote: Andorhal has been a name since Ch4 (Brask: 'the big granaries'; the ANDORHAL stencil) and a hub on paper since Ch5 (Andorhal at one end of every readable slip). This is the first sight of it. Since Ch3, the places ahead have been alive and trading while the sickness spreads through them; this is the same pattern at full scale. The party is coming in by the back way, the south road, not the King's road and its front gate. Close on Jaina facing the city, which lands POV arc bullet 4. Craft research, arrival: the city is filtered through what Jaina's body already knows, one concise picture, then out.
beats.verifierModification: Interiority adds the arc-bullet-4 turn (nobody behind her is coming; the city is in front of her). The transition is relabelled as a planted question with the Ch7 POV handoff noted.

warnings: Scene 1 is two beats of near-pure interior recognition on a riding party. B1 is carried by the plain line; B2 is sequel interior. The verifier should check that the scene has enough external pressure.
B5 and B6 are both sequels and sit after the refusal. Risk of aftermath running long right after B4's disaster. Keep tight; the outline says B6 ends the Sylvanas fight in a few lines.
B7 plants a second read (Havel cult-paid, the tally-man observing them) that Jaina's POV cannot know. Writer must render it as ordinary behaviour.
supporting.md describes Havel as harried and honest; the outline's second read makes him cult-paid in Ch7-8. Authorial divergence, flagged for the outline owner.
Strahnbrad placement relative to the Andorhal road is an authorial choice (planner memory of canon, unverified by web search).
Ch5 carried an open flag that Jaina crossing the rings unfelt is stale across five chapters; not resolved by this outline.
Outline contains two verbatim lines (B1 plague line, B7 farewell). Preserved as locked anchors, not expanded into dialogue.

chapterBridge.previousChapterClose: Ch5 ends in Sylvanas's POV at first light on day 5. At the carters' lodge at the fork, Sylvanas pins Strahnbrad with her knife and turns down Jaina's offer of a re-read ('No'). She warns that the army will put the flour after the orcs and 'Expect them to get in the way.' Jaina: 'Then I'll have to show it to them.' Sylvanas: 'You'll have to. I can't see it either.' Sylvanas folds the sheet into her coat with the slips and the sacking. The four ride out in the old order, turn south onto the bending road between the hedges, and see a long brown smear moving over the hills ahead, too brown for mist.
chapterBridge.continuityOfState: Same morning, a few hours later, the same four riders in the same order. Jaina slept sitting against a stone block for part of the night. She is grey and cold from the fork reading: right arm dead with the staff in its crook, left hand wrapped with two bare fingertips, and she ate Lyriel's burnt crust in two fingers. Sylvanas carries the sheet, the Barov slips and the ANDORHAL square. Jaina has accepted the job of showing it to the army.
chapterBridge.informationAsymmetry: This is the first time inside Jaina since Ch4. She does not know that Sylvanas thinks 'Jaina' now, that the old carter has been nagging Sylvanas, or that Cyndia turned her head at the farewell in Ch3. Sylvanas does not know the internment-camp night, or what Jaina believes her history with Arthas will buy.
chapterBridge.orientingAnchor: One anchor is enough. Either the road under the hooves, which Jaina chose and which now has to prove her right, or the brown smear ahead. Do not re-run the fork.
chapterBridge.intentionalJump: POV switch from Sylvanas back to Jaina, with a short time skip inside the same morning.

craftResearch.topic: The reasonable authority who refuses the warning
craftResearch.findings: A sympathetic obstacle has motives the reader can understand even while the harm counts. The refusal should come from visible reasons such as duty, cost, or a real competing threat, shown in what he does, not from a label or a narrator verdict.

Keep it to one moment. Enter through a present trigger with emotional weight (an object, a phrase), make it comment on or contradict the present, and exit on a present-tense jolt. Short flashbacks can sit in a fast scene if they add to the pressure.

Cut the 'she realized' frame and stage the change through behaviour, speech and body. Build pressure first, trigger the insight with a small concrete thing, and show the consequence in later choices and relationships.

A clue that is present but overlooked is fair; a withheld one is not. Conceal it among ordinary detail, follow it at once with something more pressing, and let a line with a double meaning read innocently first time.

The city's first description carries the POV character's state. Give one concise picture on arrival and then return to action. The same skyline reads as welcome or as threat depending on what the viewer already feels.

pacing.notes: Tension by beat: B1 medium, B2 medium-low, B3 medium-high, B4 high, B5 medium-high (heavy and quiet), B6 medium, B7 medium (uncanny), B8 medium-high, B9 high (dread close). One main peak at B4 (44%), a release through B5-B6, then a second, smaller climb to the close. There are never three high beats in a row. Scene lengths vary: S1 short (2 beats, B2 compressed), S2 long (4 beats), S3 medium (3 beats, B8 compressed). The risk is aftermath running long after B4, so B6 is set to compressed and given a job that is distinct from B4.

structure.notes: Scene/sequel is 6/3. That leans toward scene for a character chapter, but B7 and B8 are low-action scenes, so the felt balance is fine. The opening was at risk of being passive (an interior click on horseback). It now has a present trigger from continuity (the road read and the army on the climb) and a relational event (Sylvanas pressing on the 'show it' problem). The mid-chapter turn is B4/B5 at 44-55%. The close plants an open question: a working city, and whoever runs it is inside. Sylvanas's call about Arthas appeared twice (B4 and B6). It is now split into a prediction (B4) and a verdict with Jaina's acceptance (B6).

character.notes: Every beat filters through Jaina. Arthas is read from outside with visible reasons (orcs out of the camps). The tally-man's second read is kept as behaviour only. Agency: Jaina acts in B1 through B6. S3 risked three reactive beats in a row, so B8 now gives her a choice (she won't stop when Lyriel checks on her) and B9 closes on her facing the city. Arc bullets: POV bullet 1 was only in arcPressure and now sits in B2's decision; through-POV bullet 2 (hope that proof shows Sylvanas too cynical) is added to B3. Every bullet now lands in a beat (see arcLandingMap). Supporting functions are distinct: Sylvanas is the reader of men and armies, Lyriel is at Jaina's knee, Cyndia works the horses and stays silent on the farewell.

transitions.notes: All 9 transitionIntents are present with named causal types. B2 is re-threaded to carry the Ch5 smear into the camp. B9 is relabelled as a planted question with the Ch7 POV handoff. Cross-scene links hold: S1 ends riding into the visible war, and S2 opens in the camp; S2 ends with the horses wheeling back to the road, and S3 opens with traffic coming out of Andorhal. The chapterBridge is written from the Ch5 final prose.

continuity.notes: Fixed: (1) the evidence was in Sylvanas's coat at the Ch5 close, so Jaina's 'notes' now pass to her on the page, and she cannot write new ones; (2) S1 risked re-running Ch4's built-craft recognition as new, so it is now an evolution with a guard; (3) 'grain dust on his sleeves' would contradict Jaina's 'nothing' read and is removed; (4) 'white knuckles' is impossible with her wrapped and dead hands; (5) the Ch5 brown smear is accounted for as the army; (6) Arthas's orcs are 'out of the camps' (Ch5), which ties B5's memory to the present; (7) the tally-man must not resemble the carter, and Jaina must not draw the overseer parallel. Strahnbrad's placement is established in Ch5 memory, so the planner's canon flag is closed. The Havel divergence is reconciled by the Ch8 outline.
